claim: The minimum number of triangle-free colour classes needed to colour the edges of an uncountable complete or K4-free graph is determined; and the Erdos-Hajnal obligatory subgraph conjecture that every kappa-chromatic graph contains a kappa-chromatic triangle-free subgraph decides whether a chromatic-gap route to Erdos problem 595 can work.
domain: infinite graph theory / combinatorial set theory

facets.entities: uncountable graphs, their edge colourings with triangle-free colour classes, K4-free uncountably chromatic graphs
facets.mechanism: extremal triangle-free and odd-cycle-free edge colourings of uncountable graphs; obligatory triangle-free subgraphs of a kappa-chromatic graph
facets.method: partition calculus, forcing constructions for uncountably chromatic graphs, Hajnal-Mate graphs, diamond and CH constructions, Todorcevic walks
facets.outcome: the exact number of triangle-free colour classes needed, and whether a K4-free graph can require uncountably many
